questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I think it is important to experience other ways of studying, become stronger in English, and meet international students.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There have been many ups and downs, but experiences that I have learned from. My program has at times been very badly planned and structured, which has been very energy-consuming. Further, It's been difficult to move to new places and get a new everyday life running. But I have met the best professors, friends, nature, and culture - So it has been worth it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was pretty easy. and the professor has been very good at helping us if there was some information missing

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were a few intro days where both the student and the professor welcomed me

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think it was as good as it could be. There was information I was doubting about, but the professors were good at helping.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. There are a lot of housing opportunities here.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In Bangor everything is close so there is no bad location to stay. When you live in a house, you probably have a little more space, but campus housing is cheaper and probably more social because you often live 10 people in each apartment.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found my own little house where I lived with 3 others. We were social, it was cozy and cheap.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think Copenhagen University is very well structured. I do however study a program (SUTROFOR) that is very unknown and very few students apply. So there are often questions, that no one can answer.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Because I am a Danish student, I just had to press a button, without an application process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There are some employees in the office in Copenhagen who most often pick up the phone. They have been kind and helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I got into the classes I asked for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Read carefully - all the information is somewhere. 
Apply for private funds, it can definitely help you while studying

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In terms of me studying forestry, it is very limited how many models I have had in my first year about forestry. I would like to study more about forests. However, I had many electives models where I could control what kind of education I wanted. which I think was cool.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the different courses have overall the same degree of difficulty.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The University of Copenhagen is much more traditional teaching, with blackboard, experiments, and specific assignments - and almost only oral exams. Where Bangor University, provide teaching and assignments to the student to interpret and understand on their own. All exams are written.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Agroforestry Systems & Prac, Silviculture, and Global Food Security.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer: Dissertation project

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Agroforestry Systems & Prac, Silviculture

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are many options with clubs, bar and sports facilities

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sailing, Climbing, all kinds of ball games, Hiking, PubQuiz

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking, PubQuiz and climbing

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Snowdonia (national park)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and go to the social things. People are very nice and welcoming

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The food. They eat differently. otherwise, it is very similar to Denmark

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pub culture and the population is very kind

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. There are hard times, but it's worth it.
2. Look positively at things
3. Take advantage of the facilities both socially and professionally that are available, it makes it all a lot more fun.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have fun!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting an education I am proud of

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The professional pressure. It can be a lot sometimes.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
